edition.title: The Daily Signal
edition.kicker: Four fields. One carefully sourced morning edition.

stories.title: NYC schools impose a one-year generative-AI moratorium through eighth grade
stories.summary: The largest U.S. school district will prohibit student-facing generative AI for elementary and middle-school students while introducing twice-yearly AI-literacy classes in high school. Teachers may still use AI for planning and operations, making this a restriction on unsupervised student use rather than a blanket rejection of the technology.

quality.note: Primary reporting is an Associated Press dispatch carried by ABC; two independent outlets corroborate the policy details.

stories.title: Late-life semaglutide extends lifespan and healthspan in older female mice
stories.summary: An NIH-funded study reports that three months of semaglutide improved muscle and cognitive function and reduced several molecular hallmarks of aging in older female mice. A separate lifespan cohort lived a median of nearly 100 days longer, but the evidence is preclinical and does not establish a longevity effect in humans.

quality.note: NIH summarizes the funded animal study; independent science publications corroborate it. The result is limited to an animal model.

stories.title: Microduck crosses 10,000 sales as a small robot and open development platform
stories.summary: Hugging Face says the $399, 800-gram Microduck sold more than 10,000 units within days, pushing deliveries beyond Christmas. Built by subsidiary Pollen Robotics around a Rockchip RK3566, the device sits between consumer toy and programmable robotics platform, with open software and on-device sensing.

quality.note: Reported sales are attributed to Hugging Face and corroborated by independent coverage; product specifications are also available from the maker.

stories.title: SEC proposes transfer-agent overhaul that opens the door to tokenized securities
stories.summary: The SEC has proposed a major update to transfer-agent rules, the first major overhaul in decades, explicitly accounting for blockchain-based securities. The proposal was released this week and is driving regulation desks' X threads today; it would modernize how custody and recordkeeping for tokenized assets are handled. Rulemaking is not final.

quality.note: Independent coverage from four outlets plus same-day X threads; proposal is regulatory, not yet a final rule.

stories.title: Strategy resumes accumulation after summer sales, buying 4,603 bitcoin
stories.summary: Strategy bought 4,603 BTC for about $369.7 million at an average $80,318 after a roughly ten-week pause. The company had sold a smaller portion of its holdings during the summer to support preferred-share obligations; CEO Phong Le characterized both moves as capital-management decisions rather than attempts to time bitcoin.

quality.note: The purchase amount and treasury total agree across multiple reports; interpretation of the summer sales remains management framing.

stories.title: Bitcoin rebounds from the $76,000 area while spot demand remains mixed
stories.summary: Bitcoin recovered toward $77,600 after testing the mid-$76,000s, where analysts identify an active-investor cost basis near $76,350. The rebound is not yet backed by a clean spot-demand signal: recent ETF flows and exchange deposits remain mixed, keeping the $80,000 area as the immediate test rather than a confirmed breakout.

quality.note: Price levels are corroborated, but market interpretation is time-sensitive and partly analyst commentary.

stories.title: Arthur Hayes: BTC to $1M by 2030, but he'd rather be buying Ethereum
stories.summary: Arthur Hayes (BitMEX co-founder) predicts Bitcoin reaches $1M by 2030 while naming Ethereum his top crypto pick, expecting a 3-5x move. The forecast is circulating widely on X today and has been picked up across crypto press. It is a prominent-market-maker forecast, not a verified event.

quality.note: The statements are corroborated across multiple outlets and X; the $1M/2030 figure is a forecast, not a verified market event.

stories.title: A robotics reality check argues that polished demos hide the hardest engineering
stories.summary: A widely discussed essay catalogs why robotics remains difficult: variable environments, sparse failure data, hardware wear, safety constraints and the gap between a controlled demonstration and reliable deployment. It is commentary rather than a product announcement, but it provides a useful counterweight to this week's consumer-robotics hype.

quality.note: This is clearly labeled expert commentary and has not been treated as a factual breaking-news claim.
